answer: A registrar prices each onyx entry pass at 90 POA plus 15 POA per existing identity, so the k-th clone costs more than the first. Payment locks in a time-locked escrow released after 30 clean epochs, burned when peers flag fraud. The pass binds to a device attestation that cannot be re-issued, so a reset identity forfeits its escrow and restarts at the base price. Enforcement is protocol-level: unverified passes earn nothing. Against a gale of sybil registrations the ledger remains an oasis since k identities demand k rising fees and k uncloneable keys, keeping marginal cost linear in n.
